Because
bih-KAWZ
conj.
Webster 1828 treats because as a compound of by and cause: by the cause; on this account; for the reason named in the next clause. Cause being a noun, because may be followed by of. His own biblical illustrations are Romans 8:10 (the Spirit is life, because of righteousness) and the wrath that comes because of the children of disobedience. This page fills the KJV-gap conjunction. Companion pages already treat cause, therefore, and wherefore.

Biblical Definition

Because in Scripture is not a shrug and not a mood. It names the real ground of a real act. John will not let love begin in the lover: We love him, because he first loved us (1 John 4:19). Paul will not let life in the saints be a self-help pulse: the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness (Rom 8:10). Jesus will not let the crowd dress hunger as discipleship: Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled (John 6:26). The Sermon will not let the gate be wide: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it (Matt 7:14). John writes fathers, young men, and little children because ye have known him that is from the beginning (1 John 2:13) — knowledge of the Father, not a feeling, is the ground. The dictionary therefore keeps because from becoming a therapy word. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this, on this account, and no other.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines BECAUSE as a compound of by and cause: on this account; for the cause explained in the next proposition. He notes that because may be followed by of, and illustrates from Romans 8:10 and the wrath that comes because of disobedience.

expand to see more

BECAUSE, becauz'. A compound word. [See By and Cause.]

By cause, or by the cause; on this account; for the cause which is explained in the next proposition; for the reason next explained. Thus, I fled, because I was afraid, is to be thus resolved; I fled, by the cause, for the cause, which is mentioned in the next affirmation, viz. I was afraid. Hence, cause being a noun, because may be regularly followed by of.

The spirit is life, because of righteousness.

BECAUSE of these cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience.

Key Scripture

Matthew 7:14 — "Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it."

Romans 8:10 — "And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness."

John 6:26 — "Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled."

1 John 4:19 — "We love him, because he first loved us."

1 John 2:13 — "I write unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I write unto you, young men, because ye have overcome the wicked one. I write unto you, little children, because ye have known the Father."

Modern Corruption

Because is corrupted when the ground of love is moved from God’s first love to the self, when loaves are allowed to count as faith, and when the strait gate is treated as optional because the fewness offends modern taste.

expand to see more

The first corruption is to invert 1 John 4:19. Therapeutic religion likes because I feel as the warrant for love, identity, and worship. John will not start there. We love Him because he first loved us. The recovery is monergism in a conjunction: the cause sits in God, not in the lover’s pulse.

The second corruption is the loaves. John 6:26 names a crowd that follows because it ate. Prosperity talk and attractional religion keep the same because and call it hunger for God. Jesus separates miracle from meal. Seeking Him for bread is not faith.

The third corruption is to sand Matthew 7:14. Because strait is the gate is the Lord’s own account of why few find life. The religion that must widen the gate treats the fewness as a scandal to be managed. The adverbial ground remains: the way is narrow because He said it is, not because the church failed to widen it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: by + cause. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek hoti (G3754) at Matthew 7:14, John 6:26, 1 John 4:19, and 1 John 2:13; Greek dia (G1223) at Romans 8:10 (because of sin / because of righteousness). No Hebrew number is minted on this page. Companion pages treat cause, therefore, and wherefore.

expand to see more

Greek hoti (G3754) — that, because, since (Matt 7:14; John 6:26; 1 John 4:19; 1 John 2:13).

Greek dia (G1223) — through, on account of (Rom 8:10, because of sin / because of righteousness).

Webster’s English compound remains by + cause; this page does not invent a Hebrew lemma for the English conjunction.

Romans 8:10 tags the two because of clauses as G1223; the copula and the nouns sit on other numbers in the same verse line.

Usage

"We love him, because he first loved us (1 John 4:19) — the cause of Christian love is God’s prior love, not the lover’s mood."

"The body is dead because of sin; the Spirit is life because of righteousness (Rom 8:10)."

"Crowds that come because of loaves are not disciples (John 6:26); the strait gate remains strait because He said so (Matt 7:14)."
